semanticText:
# Bank Transfer Process Clause

Controls when a bank transfer may be requested within a Bank Transfer Contract. Its fixed `paymentPolicyAction` is `transfer`. The clause can initiate a request when a configured condition becomes eligible; completion remains a separate bank/guarantor decision.

## Configuration

- `parameters.method` defaults to `bank-transfer`; `conditional-bank` is also accepted. This validates the clause configuration and does not change `paymentTerms.method`. The containing document must satisfy Bank Transfer Contract.
- `parameters.transfer` defaults to `{}`. Its `mode` defaults to `workflow`, which adds no automatic transfer request or conditional transfer gate. The containing contract provides `requestTransfer`.
- With `parameters.transfer.mode: when`, `parameters.transfer.when` and a nonempty text `parameters.transfer.requestId` are required. Bank request execution additionally limits the identifier to 128 characters. There is no generated identifier default.
- `parameters.sources` defaults to `{}` and declares aliases used by predicate reads under `/sources/`. Referencing an undeclared alias is rejected.

The `when` predicate uses bounded, static, pure expressions. Supported operators are `$document`, `$nodeBlueId`, comparisons, `$and`, `$or`, `$not`, `$exists`, `$includes`, `$size`, `$add`, `$subtract` and `$literal`, with `list` and `val` operand fields. Document reads must use literal, non-root JSON pointers; `$nodeBlueId` must wrap a single `$document` read. Unsupported operators, dynamic paths and excessive nesting are rejected.

The policy's transition hook always rejects with `PAYMENT_PROCESS_POLICY_IMMUTABLE`. The supplied amendment preparation invokes existing clauses' transition hooks even when an amendment retains them unchanged.

## Conditional requests

In `when` mode, the plan creates `/paymentProcess_{clauseKey}/transferAllowed`, initially false, and makes `/paymentTerms/transferGate` point to it. A different pre-existing transfer gate is rejected.

Handlers reevaluate eligibility on changes to `/payment`, `/bankTransfer`, `/activation`, `/sourceLinks` and the predicate's document paths. When sources are declared, embedded-node events also trigger reevaluation. Eligibility requires `/activation/active` to equal true, the predicate result to equal true, and `/sourceLinks/ready` to equal true whenever `/clauses/documentSources` exists.

An automatic request proceeds only when that eligibility flag is true, `/payment/accepted` is true, `/payment/closed` is false and `/bankTransfer/status` is `idle`. It uses the configured request identifier and the amount and currency already stored in `paymentTerms`. Eligibility is neither a transfer outcome nor a personal permission.

The payer's `requestTransfer` operation accepts only `requestId`. Its caller must match `paymentTerms.payerChannel`; the automatic event route does not require a payer workflow call. Both routes require acceptance and applicable source readiness. A new request also requires that payment is not closed and that any configured `paymentTerms.transferGate` points to true. Thus a manual request cannot bypass an installed conditional gate.

A recorded request changes `/bankTransfer/status` to `requested` and emits `Bank Transfer Event` with `kind: Transfer Requested`, `requestId`, `amountMinor` and `currency`. It does not record transferred funds. Reusing the recorded identifier returns `duplicate`; another identifier conflicts. Duplicate requests still undergo source-readiness, caller and acceptance checks, but do not repeat the new-request closed/gate checks or emit another request.

## Bank outcomes and amounts

The configured guarantor reports outcomes through `confirmTransfer`, `declineTransfer` or `reportTransferUnknown`. Each requires the recorded `requestId` and a nonempty bank `reference` of at most 256 characters. These public operations also run `Require Active Parties`; its full admission rules are not supplied.

`confirmTransfer` additionally requires `amountMinor` and `currency` to match `paymentTerms.amountMinor` and `paymentTerms.currency` exactly. It records `completed`, sets `/payment/completed` to the instruction amount, copies the reference to `/payment/transactionId`, and emits `Payment Completed` with `evidence: bankConfirmation`. Completion does not itself set `/payment/closed`.

`declineTransfer` records terminal `declined`. `reportTransferUnknown` records unresolved `unknown`, awaiting bank reconciliation against the same request. Their optional amount and currency fields do not update confirmed funds and are not checked against the terms. New outcome transitions are allowed only from `requested` or `unknown`. Repeating the same status requires the same reference and produces no new outcome; conflicting terminal outcomes are rejected.

`acceptedNew` means a request or outcome was newly recorded, including a decline or unknown outcome. Only bank-confirmed completion establishes transferred money. This is one transfer, with no synthetic authorization or capture reservation. A refund is a separate transfer instruction, so `/payment/completed` is not a net amount after refunds.

Amounts use integer minor units of `paymentTerms.currency`. Shared payment initialization requires a positive `paymentTerms.amountMinor`, a `paymentTerms.limitMinor` at least that amount and no greater than 1,000,000,000,000, and nonempty currency text. Instruction acceptance and rejection are separate from transfer outcomes: the guarantor cannot switch an accepted instruction to rejected or vice versa; rejection requires a reason.

## Inherited connections

`bindings` can connect inherited Payment Action Definitions to `workflow`, `event`, `channel`, `change`, `embedded`, `collection`, `initialized`, `activated` or `timer` sources. These are action connections, not declared data bindings, and they do not confer bank outcome authority. Inherited financial and control request functions restricted to reservation methods do not become bank-transfer routes.

Connection `params` supplies mapped arguments, overriding action defaults; it does not implicitly copy the incoming request. Connection `when` defaults to true and skips execution when false. `parameters.conditions` adds per-action conditions, defaulting to true; a failed condition rejects execution. `before` runs before the action. `after` and completion of `once: true` run only after an `acceptedNew` result, so a duplicate can still have run `before`. `once` defaults to false.

Workflow connections require an authenticated `channel` or `party`; `request` and `event` may constrain admission. Path-based sources use non-root pointers. Embedded and collection sources arrange embedding unless `embed` is false. Timer connections require either an absolute `timestamp` in Unix microseconds or `afterEvent` with positive integer `delayMs`. Relative timers use `policy: first` by default or `latest`; initialization cannot supply their timestamp base. `cancelOn` names a cancellation source. Scheduling requires the Time runtime and does not establish that a firing occurred.

All state paths refer to the instruction document containing this clause, including when that instruction is nested. Missing state is unknown. Shared payment initialization establishes its false flags and zero amounts only after it runs. The supplied definitions do not show initialization of `/bankTransfer`; in particular, an absent status is not an established default of `idle`.
